title: api.count_cache_key
description: Key under which the invoices, customer-invoices and fees index endpoints cache their total count (BE-API-26, BE-API-27). Steps: (1) keep the endpoint's permitted parameters. Invoices: the scalar filters amount_from, amount_to, currency, invoice_type, issuing_date_from, issuing_date_to, partially_paid, payment_dispute_lost, payment_overdue, payment_status, payment_statuses, per_page, purchase_order_number, search_term, self_billed, settlements, status, statuses, plus the object `metadata` kept whole (nested values included; a non-object metadata is dropped). Fees: the scalar filters fee_type, payment_status, external_subscription_id, external_customer_id, billable_metric_code, currency, event_transaction_id and the created/failed/succeeded/refunded _from/_to bounds, plus `per_page` as given (null when absent). A scalar filter enters only when its value is a single text: a list or object given for it is dropped; unknown keys and the list filter billing_entity_codes[] are dropped (billing_entity_codes sent as a single text, even empty, enters like a scalar filter). (2) `page` never enters the key. (3) add `organization_id`. (4) turn every object into the list of its [key, value] pairs sorted by key (recursively) and serialise as compact JSON (`preimage`). key = 'pagination_count/<invoices|fees>/' + lowercase hex SHA-256 of the pre-image. The customer-scoped invoices list uses the invoices key and does not include the customer.

organization_id.description: Organization identifier (any string; the reference uses its UUID).

customer_external_id.description: Path parameter of the customer-scoped invoices list.

query.description: Query parameters as parsed from the URL: string values, arrays of strings (`k[]=v`), objects (`metadata[k]=v`).

preimage.description: Exact JSON text that was hashed.
